text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong says with People's Action Party holding 81 of 83 seats in parliament, goverment must look for ways to ensure different viewpoints are aired.
- National soccer midfielder Nazri Nasir in hospital after being struck by mystery illness.
- Singapore businessman shot dead at his aluminium reprocessing factory in Johor, Malaysia on Saturday.
- NTUC income hopes to grow fledgling reverse mortage business to between 15 and 20 percent of its local funds in about 15 years' time, chief executive Tan Kin Lian says.
- Taiwan regulators say they do not rule out possibility of cutting data supply to futures exchanges in Chicago and Singapore after six-month review.
- Post Office Savings Bank forecasts net surplus of Singapore $100 million at the bank level for this year, up from projected S$80 million last year.
- Majority of Asian stock markets should take their cue this week from latest twists and turns in U.S. stocks.
- Initial Public Offer fever continues strong, with three expected this week and another three by end of month.
- Foreign institutional investors ploughed record sums into Taiwanese stocks in 1996, and expected to continue to show strong interest this year.
- Slew of companies expected to seek listing on Hong Kong stock market in first quarter of 1997.
- Five of world's leading information technology vendors come together to form a global Internet training and certification consortium.
- Malaysia's stock market could see hefty gains in 1997, underpinned by political stability and a moderating economuy.
- Tenaga Nasional Bhd plans to raise further US$1 billion from the market, both local and foreign, during first quarter of year.
